NASB.1: 'Can you draw out Leviathan with a fishhook? Or press down his tongue with a cord?
NASB.2: 'Can you put a rope in his nose Or pierce his jaw with a hook?
NASB.3: 'Will he make many supplications to you, Or will he speak to you soft words?
NASB.4: 'Will he make a covenant with you? Will you take him for a servant forever?
NASB.5: 'Will you play with him as with a bird, Or will you bind him for your maidens?
NASB.6: 'Will the traders bargain over him? Will they divide him among the merchants?
NASB.7: 'Can you fill his skin with harpoons, Or his head with fishing spears?
NASB.8: 'Lay your hand on him; Remember the battle; you will not do it again!
NASB.9: 'Behold, your expectation is false; Will you be laid low even at the sight of him?
NASB.10: 'No one is so fierce that he dares to arouse him; Who then is he that can stand before Me?
NASB.11: 'Who has given to Me that I should repay [him]? [Whatever] is under the whole heaven is Mine.
NASB.12: 'I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, Or his mighty strength, or his orderly frame.
NASB.13: 'Who can strip off his outer armor? Who can come within his double mail?
NASB.14: 'Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth there is terror.
NASB.15: '[His] strong scales are [his] pride, Shut up [as with] a tight seal.
NASB.16: 'One is so near to another That no air can come between them.
NASB.17: 'They are joined one to another; They clasp each other and cannot be separated.
NASB.18: 'His sneezes flash forth light, And his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
NASB.19: 'Out of his mouth go burning torches; Sparks of fire leap forth.
NASB.20: 'Out of his nostrils smoke goes forth As [from] a boiling pot and [burning] rushes.
NASB.21: 'His breath kindles coals, And a flame goes forth from his mouth.
NASB.22: 'In his neck lodges strength, And dismay leaps before him.
NASB.23: 'The folds of his flesh are joined together, Firm on him and immovable.
NASB.24: 'His heart is as hard as a stone, Even as hard as a lower millstone.
NASB.25: 'When he raises himself up, the mighty fear; Because of the crashing they are bewildered.
NASB.26: 'The sword that reaches him cannot avail, Nor the spear, the dart or the javelin.
NASB.27: 'He regards iron as straw, Bronze as rotten wood.
NASB.28: 'The arrow cannot make him flee; Slingstones are turned into stubble for him.
NASB.29: 'Clubs are regarded as stubble; He laughs at the rattling of the javelin.
NASB.30: 'His underparts are [like] sharp potsherds; He spreads out [like] a threshing sledge on the mire.
NASB.31: 'He makes the depths boil like a pot; He makes the sea like a jar of ointment.
NASB.32: 'Behind him he makes a wake to shine; One would think the deep to be gray-haired.
NASB.33: 'Nothing on earth is like him, One made without fear.
NASB.34: 'He looks on everything that is high; He is king over all the sons of pride.'

ESV.1: “Can you draw out Leviathan  with a fishhook or press down his tongue with a cord?
ESV.2: Can you put a rope in his nose or pierce his jaw with a hook?
ESV.3: Will he make many pleas to you? Will he speak to you soft words?
ESV.4: Will he make a covenant with you to take him for your servant forever?
ESV.5: Will you play with him as with a bird, or will you put him on a leash for your girls?
ESV.6: Will traders bargain over him? Will they divide him up among the merchants?
ESV.7: Can you fill his skin with harpoons or his head with fishing spears?
ESV.8: Lay your hands on him; remember the battle — you will not do it again!
ESV.9: Behold, the hope of a man is false; he is laid low even at the sight of him.
ESV.10: No one is so fierce that he dares to stir him up. Who then is he who can stand before me?
ESV.11: Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Whatever is under the whole heaven is mine.
ESV.12: “I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, or his mighty strength, or his goodly frame.
ESV.13: Who can strip off his outer garment? Who would come near him with a bridle?
ESV.14: Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.
ESV.15: His back is made of  rows of shields, shut up closely as with a seal.
ESV.16: One is so near to another that no air can come between them.
ESV.17: They are joined one to another; they clasp each other and cannot be separated.
ESV.18: His sneezings flash forth light, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the dawn.
ESV.19: Out of his mouth go flaming torches; sparks of fire leap forth.
ESV.20: Out of his nostrils comes forth smoke, as from a boiling pot and burning rushes.
ESV.21: His breath kindles coals, and a flame comes forth from his mouth.
ESV.22: In his neck abides strength, and terror dances before him.
ESV.23: The folds of his flesh stick together, firmly cast on him and immovable.
ESV.24: His heart is hard as a stone, hard as the lower millstone.
ESV.25: When he raises himself up, the mighty  are afraid; at the crashing they are beside themselves.
ESV.26: Though the sword reaches him, it does not avail, nor the spear, the dart, or the javelin.
ESV.27: He counts iron as straw, and bronze as rotten wood.
ESV.28: The arrow cannot make him flee; for him, sling stones are turned to stubble.
ESV.29: Clubs are counted as stubble; he laughs at the rattle of javelins.
ESV.30: His underparts are like sharp potsherds; he spreads himself like a threshing sledge on the mire.
ESV.31: He makes the deep boil like a pot; he makes the sea like a pot of ointment.
ESV.32: Behind him he leaves a shining wake; one would think the deep to be white-haired.
ESV.33: On earth there is not his like, a creature without fear.
ESV.34: He sees everything that is high; he is king over all the sons of pride.”

NLT.1:
“Can you catch Leviathan with a hook
or put a noose around its jaw?
NLT.2:
Can you tie it with a rope through the nose
or pierce its jaw with a spike?
NLT.3:
Will it beg you for mercy
or implore you for pity?
NLT.4:
Will it agree to work for you,
to be your slave for life?
NLT.5:
Can you make it a pet like a bird,
or give it to your little girls to play with?
NLT.6:
Will merchants try to buy it
to sell it in their shops?
NLT.7:
Will its hide be hurt by spears
or its head by a harpoon?
NLT.8:
If you lay a hand on it,
you will certainly remember the battle that follows.
You won’t try that again!
NLT.9:
No, it is useless to try to capture it.
The hunter who attempts it will be knocked down.
NLT.10:
And since no one dares to disturb it,
who then can stand up to me?
NLT.11:
Who has given me anything that I need to pay back?
Everything under heaven is mine.
NLT.12:
“I want to emphasize Leviathan’s limbs
and its enormous strength and graceful form.
NLT.13:
Who can strip off its hide,
and who can penetrate its double layer of armor?
NLT.14:
Who could pry open its jaws?
For its teeth are terrible!
NLT.15:
The scales on its back are like rows of shields
tightly sealed together.
NLT.16:
They are so close together
that no air can get between them.
NLT.17:
Each scale sticks tight to the next.
They interlock and cannot be penetrated.
NLT.18:
“When it sneezes, it flashes light!
Its eyes are like the red of dawn.
NLT.19:
Lightning leaps from its mouth;
flames of fire flash out.
NLT.20:
Smoke streams from its nostrils
like steam from a pot heated over burning rushes.
NLT.21:
Its breath would kindle coals,
for flames shoot from its mouth.
NLT.22:
“The tremendous strength in Leviathan’s neck
strikes terror wherever it goes.
NLT.23:
Its flesh is hard and firm
and cannot be penetrated.
NLT.24:
Its heart is hard as rock,
hard as a millstone.
NLT.25:
When it rises, the mighty are afraid,
gripped by terror.
NLT.26:
No sword can stop it,
no spear, dart, or javelin.
NLT.27:
Iron is nothing but straw to that creature,
and bronze is like rotten wood.
NLT.28:
Arrows cannot make it flee.
Stones shot from a sling are like bits of grass.
NLT.29:
Clubs are like a blade of grass,
and it laughs at the swish of javelins.
NLT.30:
Its belly is covered with scales as sharp as glass.
It plows up the ground as it drags through the mud.
NLT.31:
“Leviathan makes the water boil with its commotion.
It stirs the depths like a pot of ointment.
NLT.32:
The water glistens in its wake,
making the sea look white.
NLT.33:
Nothing on earth is its equal,
no other creature so fearless.
NLT.34:
Of all the creatures, it is the proudest.
It is the king of beasts.”

NIV.1:
“Can you pull in the leviathan with a fishhook
or tie down his tongue with a rope?
NIV.2:
Can you put a cord through his nose
or pierce his jaw with a hook?
NIV.3:
Will he keep begging you for mercy?
Will he speak to you with gentle words?
NIV.4:
Will he make an agreement with you
for you to take him as your slave for life?
NIV.5:
Can you make a pet of him like a bird
or put him on a leash for your girls?
NIV.6:
Will traders barter for him?
Will they divide him up among the merchants?
NIV.7:
Can you fill his hide with harpoons
or his head with fishing spears?
NIV.8:
If you lay a hand on him,
you will remember the struggle and never do it again!
NIV.9:
Any hope of subduing him is false;
the mere sight of him is overpowering.
NIV.10:
No one is fierce enough to rouse him.
Who then is able to stand against me?
NIV.11:
Who has a claim against me that I must pay?
Everything under heaven belongs to me.
NIV.12:
“I will not fail to speak of his limbs,
his strength and his graceful form.
NIV.13:
Who can strip off his outer coat?
Who would approach him with a bridle?
NIV.14:
Who dares open the doors of his mouth,
ringed about with his fearsome teeth?
NIV.15:
His back has rows of shields
tightly sealed together;
NIV.16:
each is so close to the next
that no air can pass between.
NIV.17:
They are joined fast to one another;
they cling together and cannot be parted.
NIV.18:
His snorting throws out flashes of light;
his eyes are like the rays of dawn.
NIV.19:
Firebrands stream from his mouth;
sparks of fire shoot out.
NIV.20:
Smoke pours from his nostrils
as from a boiling pot over a fire of reeds.
NIV.21:
His breath sets coals ablaze,
and flames dart from his mouth.
NIV.22:
Strength resides in his neck;
dismay goes before him.
NIV.23:
The folds of his flesh are tightly joined;
they are firm and immovable.
NIV.24:
His chest is hard as rock,
hard as a lower millstone.
NIV.25:
When he rises up, the mighty are terrified;
they retreat before his thrashing.
NIV.26:
The sword that reaches him has no effect,
nor does the spear or the dart or the javelin.
NIV.27:
Iron he treats like straw
and bronze like rotten wood.
NIV.28:
Arrows do not make him flee;
slingstones are like chaff to him.
NIV.29:
A club seems to him but a piece of straw;
he laughs at the rattling of the lance.
NIV.30:
His undersides are jagged potsherds,
leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.
NIV.31:
He makes the depths churn like a boiling caldron
and stirs up the sea like a pot of ointment.
NIV.32:
Behind him he leaves a glistening wake;
one would think the deep had white hair.
NIV.33:
Nothing on earth is his equal—
a creature without fear.
NIV.34:
He looks down on all that are haughty;
he is king over all that are proud.”

MSG.1:
"Or can you pull in the sea beast, Leviathan, with a fly rod
and stuff him in your creel?
MSG.2:
Can you lasso him with a rope,
or snag him with an anchor?
MSG.3:
Will he beg you over and over for mercy,
or flatter you with flowery speech?
MSG.4:
Will he apply for a job with you
to run errands and serve you the rest of your life?
MSG.5:
Will you play with him as if he were a pet goldfish?
Will you make him the mascot of the neighborhood children?
MSG.6:
Will you put him on display in the market
and have shoppers haggle over the price?
MSG.7:
Could you shoot him full of arrows like a pin cushion,
or drive harpoons into his huge head?
MSG.8:
If you so much as lay a hand on him,
you won't live to tell the story.
MSG.9:
What hope would you have with such a creature?
Why, one look at him would do you in!
MSG.10:
If you can't hold your own against his glowering visage,
how, then, do you expect to stand up to me?
MSG.11:
Who could confront me and get by with it?
I'm in charge of all this—I run this universe!
MSG.12:
"But I've more to say about Leviathan, the sea beast,
his enormous bulk, his beautiful shape.
MSG.13:
Who would even dream of piercing that tough skin
or putting those jaws into bit and bridle?
MSG.14:
And who would dare knock at the door of his mouth
filled with row upon row of fierce teeth?
MSG.15:
His pride is invincible;
nothing can make a dent in that pride.
MSG.16:
Nothing can get through that proud skin—
impervious to weapons and weather,
MSG.17:
The thickest and toughest of hides,
impenetrable!
MSG.18:
"He snorts and the world lights up with fire,
he blinks and the dawn breaks.
MSG.19:
Comets pour out of his mouth,
fireworks arc and branch.
MSG.20:
Smoke erupts from his nostrils
like steam from a boiling pot.
MSG.21:
He blows and fires blaze;
flames of fire stream from his mouth.
MSG.22:
All muscle he is—sheer and seamless muscle.
To meet him is to dance with death.
MSG.23:
Sinewy and lithe,
there's not a soft spot in his entire body—
MSG.24:
As tough inside as out,
rock-hard, invulnerable.
MSG.25:
Even angels run for cover when he surfaces,
cowering before his tail-thrashing turbulence.
MSG.26:
Javelins bounce harmlessly off his hide,
harpoons ricochet wildly.
MSG.27:
Iron bars are so much straw to him,
bronze weapons beneath notice.
MSG.28:
Arrows don't even make him blink;
bullets make no more impression than raindrops.
MSG.29:
A battle ax is nothing but a splinter of kindling;
he treats a brandished harpoon as a joke.
MSG.30:
His belly is armor-plated, inexorable—
unstoppable as a barge.
MSG.31:
He roils deep ocean the way you'd boil water,
he whips the sea like you'd whip an egg into batter.
MSG.32:
With a luminous trail stretching out behind him,
you might think Ocean had grown a gray beard!
MSG.33:
There's nothing on this earth quite like him,
not an ounce of fear in that creature!
MSG.34:
He surveys all the high and mighty—
king of the ocean, king of the deep!"

NET.23: The folds of its flesh are tightly joined; they are firm on it, immovable.
NET.24: Its heart is hard as rock, hard as a lower millstone.
